title: Hong Kong man arrested on return to Changi Airport over alleged shop theft 3 months earlier

 singapore Hong Kong man arrested on return to Changi Airport over alleged shop theft 3 months earlier
 The 38-year-old man will be charged in court on Tuesday (Nov 17) The transit area of Changi Airport Terminal 1. PHOTO: TA.LE Architects PUBLISHED ON November 16, 2026 7:28 PM BY Sean Ler The long arm of the law caught up with a 38-year-old Hong Kong man on Oct 29, some three months after he allegedly stole a box of earbuds from a retail outlet in the transit area of Changi Airport Terminal 1.
 In a news release on Monday (16 Nov), police said the alleged incident took place at about 12.30pm on Aug 2.
 His alleged crime came to light after a retail assistant discovered a box of earbuds missing from the display shelf when she conducted a stock check.
 The retail assistant then reviewed the store's closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage and established that the man had taken the earbuds valued at $347.71 at about 10.20am and left the premises without paying.
 Officers from the Airport Police Division established the man's identity with the CCTV footage but he had already departed.
 He was eventually arrested in a planned police operation during his transit through Changi Airport on Oct 29.
 The 38-year-old will be charged in court on Tuesday with the offence of theft in dwelling. If found guilty of the said offence, he could be jailed for up to seven years, fined, or both.
 The police reiterated that it takes a serious view of shop theft cases, adding that they will deal firmly with offenders in accordance with the law.
 "Offenders should not assume that they can evade detection after committing such offences. The Police will continue to work closely with airport stakeholders to prevent, detect, and deter shop theft at Changi Airport," they added.
